mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days. The relationship is linear and negative: as FEDFUNDS decreases, returns increase.
failure_condition: The average 5-day SPX return is negative when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0% (as of t-1mo), or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% over a 3-month window signals an impending recession, causing investors to sell equities and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a severe economic contraction, prompting a flight to safety and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day SPX return is positive when FEDFUNDS decreases and UNRATE increases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a housing market expansion (HOUST > 1400 thousand units), the S&P 500 experiences positive forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased consumer spending and business investment.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months when HOUST > 1400, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 over a 3-month period signals an economic contraction, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of total nonfarm employment (PAYEMS) compresses the risk premium on equities by signaling robust economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day SPX return is negative when PAYEMS is above 155,000 thousand, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of weak real GDP growth (GDPC1 below 1.5% annualized) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL above 3.0%) signals stagflation, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day SPX return is positive when GDPC1 < 1.5% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0%, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a period of strong consumer spending (RSAFS > 700,000 million dollars), the S&P 500 experiences positive forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to robust corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months when RSAFS > 700000, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
